name: ramose
description: Ramose — an immutable, Datomic-inspired graph database for Cloudflare (Workers + Durable Objects + R2), built on Effect. One package: the schema and client (`ramose/db`), the Alchemy resources (`ramose`), the peer Worker (`ramose/worker`), the React hooks (`ramose/react`) and the Better Auth plugins (`ramose/better-auth`).
author: Tyler van Hensbergen <tvanhens@gmail.com>
//dependencies: Ramose owns its whole runtime graph on purpose: `bun add ramose` has to be
enough. Two of these ranges are load-bearing rather than incidental.
`effect` — a bare `effect` in a consumer's manifest installs 3.x, which is
the wrong major and typechecks against nothing here. Owning the dependency
with a prerelease floor is what makes the Effect 4 line resolve without the
consumer ever typing `effect@rc`. The floor carries a prerelease tag so
semver admits the other 4.0.0 prereleases; `<5.0.0` keeps the next major
out.
Effect types cross the public API boundary (a `Db` is parameterised by
`Schema`s, a live query is a `Stream`), so two copies of `effect` in one
tree do not merely duplicate bytes — they produce two mutually unassignable
sets of types and nothing typechecks. The mitigation is that a consumer
never has to name `effect` at all: it arrives under `ramose`, and the
`ramose/effect` and `ramose/schema` subpaths re-export the same module
instances for resolvers that do not hoist (pnpm's default, Yarn PnP). A
consumer who *does* add `effect` to their own manifest should use a range
compatible with this one; anything else is the one way back to two copies.
`alchemy` is a real dependency, not a peer: it also carries the `alchemy`
CLI the quickstart runs, and a peer would put its installation back on the
consumer. React stays an optional peer — a server-only app needs none of it
— and so does `better-auth`, which only `ramose/better-auth` touches.
